BH3 profiling (functional apoptosis testing) (simple)
records.text: A laboratory test that measures how a cell's mitochondria respond to defined challenges. This helps researchers study readiness for cell death; it does not by itself establish which treatment will help a patient.

records.name: Cell line (simple)
records.text: A population of cells maintained through repeated transfers in laboratory culture. Its origin, identity and growth conditions affect what it can model.

records.name: Cell lines as a proxy for patients (simple)
CRISPR functional genomics (simple)
records.text: Knocking out every gene one by one in cancer cells to find the ones they cannot live without.

records.name: Cancer cell line encyclopedias and dependency maps (simple)
records.text: Cancer cell line encyclopedias are large public collections of cancer cells profiled for their genomes, drug sensitivity and gene dependencies, used to find new targets.

records.name: Functional (ex vivo) drug testing (simple)
records.text: Testing medicines on collected living cells or tissue under laboratory conditions. The result describes that sample and experiment; whether using it improves care needs separate evidence.

records.name: Ex vivo drug sensitivity screening in blood cancers (EXALT) (simple)
records.text: Testing drug responses in collected blood-cancer cells. A result needs the sample, assay and study context; a clinical study of one selection method does not validate every screen.

records.name: Organoid (simple)
records.text: A three-dimensional culture that organises selected features of a tissue. A tumour organoid is one type, and its contents need checking before researchers use it to answer a question.

records.name: Patient-derived organoids (simple)
records.text: Cultures grown from a patient's tumour to study selected tissue features and drug responses. They do not recreate the whole patient, and their intended use needs its own evidence.

records.name: Patient-derived xenografts (simple)
records.text: A patient's tumour grown in a mouse, used to test drugs before they are tried in people.

records.name: Model organism (simple)
records.text: A model organism is a species studied in the lab, mice above all, to understand biology shared with humans and to test cancer drugs, imperfectly.

records.name: Tumour spheroid models (hanging-drop and ultra-low-attachment culture) (simple)
Ex vivo tumour fragments and slices (simple)
Tumour-on-a-chip (simple)
records.text: A small engineered culture device for studying selected tumour interactions. Its cells, channels and conditions vary by design and must be measured.

records.name: In vitro and in vivo (simple)
records.text: Check whether a result was measured in a laboratory, removed living tissue, a living animal or person, or a computer model. Each setting includes and leaves out different things.
